text:
Alex: Heads-up — I ran a 1h host-side streaming stress against canary model v2-quant and saw a sustained latency tail starting at ~11:23 UTC. CPU on the host parse + decode threads spiked, and the allocator churn looks like backpressure from framing.
Maria: Can you paste the perf trace/profile? Which component burned the most cycles?
Alex: Dumping the relevant slice. Key bits: heavy read loops in stream_framer, then stall in preparse where we try to assemble chunk headers. KVcache ops spike after fallback to small-batch kernel selection.

```
# short trace excerpt (timestamps relative)
11:22:58 readv loop  ->  120ms
11:23:01 frame_parse   ->  340ms (grow buf)
11:23:01 preparse.kv  ->  210ms (kv miss thrash)
11:23:02 kernel_select->  95ms (fallback path)
11:23:02 decode queue ->  480ms (queued due to small batch)
```

Alex: The interesting bit is decode queue latency correlated with many tiny streaming chunks (50-200B). When batching heuristics see many in-flight short requests, kernel selector picks a smaller kernel leading to lower throughput and higher host-side CPU.
Sam: Huh. Could be our frame coalescer is not aggressive enough for connections with Nagle off. Are these clients using http2 trailers or chunked-stream? That pattern matters.
Alex: Mostly gRPC over HTTP/2 with many tiny messages (token-by-token style testing from a lab harness). I think the root is twofold: 1) framer isn't coalescing from the socket before parse, 2) KV cache eviction thrash while we fallback to a narrow kernel and cold kv sets.

Jen: Do we have a canary with coalescing enabled? I remember a flag stream_coalesce_ms in the shim that we recently rolled back for latency spikes.
Alex: Yeah we briefly enabled coalesce=5ms in canary but reverted. I re-enabled locally with 8ms and ran the same harness — queueing dropped ~30%, throughput up ~12%.

perf-bot: Canary deployment note: canary/402 -> stream_coalesce=8ms enabled at 11:40 UTC for test cluster. Observability traces attached in dashboard.

Maria: Nice. Two follow-ups: a) can you share host-level pprof and flamegraph for preparse thread? b) can we simulate KVcache hot-shard and confirm eviction policy's role?
Alex: Uploaded a minimal flamegraph link: https://internal/captures/93711122/fg.svg — main hotspot: parse::read_iter -> frame::grow -> kv::get_or_load -> allocator::slow_path

Sam: For KV cache, is eviction LRU-based? If small batches reduce locality, we may be filling more shards leading to cross-shard locks.
Alex: It's sharded LRU with per-shard lock. Under tiny-chunk load the shard distribution gets skewed; we get lock contention and repeated misses. That explains the kv miss spike.

Jen: Proposed quick mitigations:
- bump stream_coalesce_ms to 8-10ms for canary traffic
- add a short-running prefetch for likely KV prefixes on new connections
- adjust batching heuristic: prefer to accumulate up to 1kB or 5ms window for gRPC streaming inputs

Alex: Experiment notes: with coalesce=8ms + batching window 5ms we saw median latency stable and 95th drop by ~18%. CPU increased slightly in kernel selection but net tokens/sec improved.

Maria: Sounds promising. Action items:
- Alex to open a lightweight RFC with measurement artifacts + config patch (coalesce + batching tweak)
- Sam to run KV-shard skew sim and propose change to shard assignment or eviction to reduce lock blowups
- Jen to coordinate a controlled canary (10%) and attach rollout guard in console (fallback to previous coalesce on error)

Alex: Will do. I'll include a snippet of the minimal change for the framer (pseudo):

```
// framer: coalesce small reads for up to N ms or until size >= threshold
if (pending_bytes < COALESCE_MIN && elapsed < coalesce_ms) {
  wait_for_more_data(timeout=coalesce_ms - elapsed);
}
parse(pending_buffer);
```

Sam: Also add a metric for "coalesced_bytes_per_conn" so we can tune without guessing.
Jen: Agreed. I'll add the rollback policy to the canary runbook.
perf-bot: Note: create ticket PERF-1428 for RFC + measurements.

Alex: Thanks all — I'll open the RFC and kick off the sim. If anyone wants to pair on the KV sim, ping me.
Maria: Pinged. I'll review the RFC once it's up. :thumbsup:
